doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Weekly work and the trio at Jazz at Pearl's
summary: He plays three nights a week at Jazz at Pearl's, begun with Sonny Buxton and Pearl Wong, with rotating pianists and guitarists.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What’s a typical week like for you in this area? I mean most musicians need to do a lot of different things. Is that the case for you?

Yes. I’m fortunate in that I’ve been involved in this one little club called Jazz at Pearl’s which is the local jazz club — by local, they use local musicians. It’s not like Yoshi’s across the Bay is the national, or the international club. People come from all over the world to play Yoshi’s. But Jazz at Pearl’s is our little neighborhood jazz club and I came with the place twelve years ago. So you’ve probably — that’s why you’ve seen my name. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
I think I’ve seen your name.

I’m there three nights a week. He just gave it to me. You know I started out, I worked for this Sonny Buxton, who is somebody you should talk to I think maybe. Anyway Sonny is a very interesting man. He had a former club called Milestones. I worked there. And when he and Pearl Wong opened this club twelve years ago they didn’t know what they were going to do on weeknights. On weekends they knew what they wanted to do. So I started playing, taking a little trio in there on weeknights. And it was sort of week to week. And then after a few weeks or months he just said why don’t you just let me know when you can’t be here.
Oh I like those kind of gigs. I have one at home actually.

Oh yeah? You know what I’m talking about. I mean and so I did it with Bruce Forman, a great guitarist for several years because we were neighbors. And then he left the area, he’s now living in Carmel Valley. So he’s not available. And I had another piano player right after him for several years. So in other words I had the same guys. And then Al Plank is this piano player, this wonderful musician. And he had some surgery last I guess December and he’s recovered but he just doesn’t want to do anything right now. He’s just kind of taking a little hiatus. So I’ve been using different people, or I should say the club owner books different people. So every night I’ll walk in and play with a different piano player or guitar player. And there’s like a pool of people. And so it’s very interesting. I get the bass player and it’s right down the street from my house, you know I’ve kind of died and went to Birdland.
Great. I’ll have to see if I can get in there before we leave here.
It’s probably close to this area.
Yeah it’s Columbus Avenue. You go I guess it would be west — or east rather — you go the other way. And it’s right near the heart of North Beach.
